nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $G$ be normalized density families on a measurable space $\Omega$ with the same parameter set $\Theta$ and the same dominating measure $\mu$. If for every $\theta \in \Theta$ and every $x \in \Omega$ the density of $F$ at $\theta$ and the density of $G$ at $\theta$ take the same value at $x$, then $F = G$.
nodes.title: Normalized density families are determined by their densities

nodes.summary: For a normalized density family $F$, every parameter $\theta$ and the empty sample $x$ (sample size $n = 0$), the iid likelihood of $\theta$ at $x$ equals $1$, the empty product.
nodes.title: Likelihood of the empty sample

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$ and densities $f_\theta$ for $\theta \in \Theta$. For a sample size $n$, a parameter $\theta \in \Theta$ and a sample $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \in \Omega^n$, the iid likelihood of $\theta$ at $x$ is $L_n(\theta; x) = \prod_{i < n} f_\theta(x_i)$, a value in $[0, \infty]$. For $n = 0$ this is the empty product $1$.
nodes.title: Likelihood of an iid sample

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, let $n$ be a sample size, let $\tau : \Theta \to H$ be a map into a set $H$, and let $x \in \Omega^n$ be a sample. For $\eta$ in the image of $\tau$, the induced likelihood of $\eta$ at $x$ is the supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the iid likelihood $L_n(\theta; x)$ over the fiber of $\tau$ above $\eta$:
nodes.title: Induced likelihood

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, let $n$ be a sample size, let $L_n(\theta; x)$ denote the iid likelihood of $\theta \in \Theta$ at a sample $x \in \Omega^n$, and let $\hat\theta$ be a map from $\Omega^n$ to $\Theta$. Then $\hat\theta$ is a maximum likelihood estimator for samples of size $n$ if and only if $L_n(\theta; x) \le L_n(\hat\theta(x); x)$ for every sample…
nodes.title: Characterization of maximum likelihood estimators

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, let $n$ be a sample size, and let $L_n(\theta; x)$ denote the iid likelihood of $\theta \in \Theta$ at a sample $x \in \Omega^n$. A map $\hat\theta$ from $\Omega^n$ to $\Theta$ is a maximum likelihood estimator for samples of size $n$ if for every sample $x \in \Omega^n$ the parameter $\hat\theta(x)$ maximizes…
nodes.title: Maximum likelihood estimator

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, dominating measure $\mu$ and densities $f_\theta$. For every $\theta \in \Theta$, the population law $P_\theta$, the measure with density $f_\theta$ with respect to $\mu$, is a probability measure.
nodes.title: Population laws are probability measures

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a normalized density family on a measurable space $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, dominating measure $\mu$ and densities $f_\theta$. The population law at $\theta \in \Theta$ is the measure $P_\theta$ on $\Omega$ with density $f_\theta$ with respect to $\mu$, so that $P_\theta(A) = \int_A f_\theta \, d\mu$ for every measurable set $A \subseteq \Omega$.
nodes.title: Population law

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space with a measure $\mu$ and let $\Theta$ be a set of parameters. A normalized density family on $\Omega$ indexed by $\Theta$ with dominating measure $\mu$ consists of a function $f_\theta : \Omega \to [0, \infty]$ for each $\theta \in \Theta$ such that $f_\theta$ is $\mu$-almost everywhere measurable and $\int_\Omega f_\theta \, d\mu = 1$.
nodes.title: Normalized density family
